title: Point-in-Time Correct Feature Joins
summary: Build training data the way a feature store does: join each label to the latest feature values known at that moment, respect a TTL, detect leakage, and do it fast enough for millions of rows.

hints.test_joins_latest_feature_at_or_before_e: For each label, take the feature row with the largest feature_ts that is <= event_ts. Rows with equal timestamps count, because they were already known.
hints.test_never_uses_future_features: Anything with feature_ts > event_ts didn't exist yet at prediction time. Using it is target leakage.
hints.test_missing_entity_or_no_history_gives_: No feature row at or before the event means features=None and feature_ts=None. Don't fall back to a future row.
hints.test_ttl_expires_stale_features: With a ttl, treat a match where event_ts − feature_ts > ttl as missing (features=None).
hints.test_ties_prefer_last_written: When two feature rows share an entity and feature_ts, the one that appears later in the input wins, like a later write.
hints.test_output_order_and_shape: Return one row per label, in the original label order: {**label, 'feature_ts': ts or None, 'features': {...} or None}.
hints.test_inputs_not_mutated: Build new dicts. Don't add keys to the caller's label dicts or sort their lists in place.
hints.test_detect_leakage: Return the indices of rows where feature_ts is not None and feature_ts > event_ts.
hints.test_scales_to_large_inputs: Comparing every label with every feature is O(n·m). Group features by entity, sort each group by timestamp once, then use bisect_right to find the match in O(log m).
